series.title: Moon Vessels
series.description: Large porcelain jars thrown in two halves and joined at the belly. The seam is left to settle in the kiln, so no two profiles close in quite the same way.

series.title: Flow
series.description: Tall forms made as a surface for glaze to travel down. Copper, iron and titanium are layered thickly at the rim and allowed to run until the kiln cools.

series.title: Tide Bowls
series.description: Open forms carrying celadon and ash glazes that pool where the wall thins. Each bowl records the level the glaze reached before the fire stopped it.

series.title: Ash & Stone
series.description: Storage jars fired for five days in a wood kiln. No glaze is applied; the colour is fly ash from the firebox, melted onto whichever shoulder faced the flame.

series.title: Ember
series.description: Hand-built tea bowls and small jars pulled from the kiln while still glowing. Iron reds and carbon blacks are drawn by smoke rather than brush.

series.title: Night Bowls
series.description: Tea bowls in iron-saturated black glaze. Held to the light, the surface breaks into fine brown streaks where the iron has risen and cooled.

series.title: Quiet Forms
series.description: Single vessels made between larger bodies of work. Each one tests a glaze, a profile or a carving before it is carried into a series.
